title: Resource commitment & autoscale OKR planning for Dedicated capacity (quarterly governance)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define and lock the Q1 roadmap and OKRs that govern Dedicated capacity commitments, autoscaling behavior, and pricing governance for enterprise customers. This ticket coordinates cross-functional requirements for capacity SLAs, burst policies, pricing guardrails, rollout cadence, and telemetry needed to measure unit economics. Scope includes: 1) OKR definition and target metrics for committed capacity uptake, average utilization, and cost-per-token improvements from autoscale optimizations; 2) Governance rules for committed vs. burst capacity (reservation windows, billing treatment, fallback models); 3) Required product and infra deliverables for Q1 (canary policy, capacity dashboard, billing mapping); 4) Ops runbooks and guardrails for emergency scale-downs and customer communication playbooks; 5) Pricing experiment plan and legal/contract template updates for committed capacity seats. Out of scope: deep runtime kernel changes and model-level quantization recommendations (tracked separately with ENG-3024).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Written OKRs and target metrics published to team Confluence and linked in ticket.
2) Capacity governance doc (reservation + burst rules) approved by finance and legal.
3) Implementation plan with milestones and owners for: canary policy, capacity dashboard, billing mapping, runbooks.
4) End-to-end telemetry plan (data sources, dashboards, alert thresholds) signed off by Observability.
5) Pricing experiment design complete and scheduled for legal review.
success_metrics:
- Committed capacity sales conversion rate >= 12% for targeted accounts by end of Q1.
- Median Dedicated utilization increase of 10% (due to improved autoscale policy & governance).
- Per-token serving cost reduction of 8% in dedicated workloads attributed to autoscale tuning.
- <1 customer-facing incident caused by autoscale policy changes during rollout.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Customers experience unexpected throttling when burst policies change. Mitigation: run two-wave canary (internal + friendly customers) with explicit communication and auto-fallback to prior policy for 24h.
Risk: Billing disputes from unclear mapping of committed vs burst usage. Mitigation: finance/contracting review of billing mapping doc and create sample invoices in sandbox.
Risk: Infra dependency delays (ENG-2911). Mitigation: identify minimum viable telemetry and delay noncritical dashboard features to post-launch.
